scope: Original fictional worked examples for P05-L02 research. No field measurements, real recommendation, runtime lesson or agronomic validation.
units: inches of water; capacity per depth is inches/inch
assumptions: Fixed uniform management zone; no capillary rise or changing root depth.
All rain in these exercises is effective; rain runoff is zero.
Irrigation efficiency converts gross application to water retained in the managed zone. The same loss is not added again to the net-input balance.
Within a day, inputs and estimated crop use are netted. Any remaining excess is removed immediately at the boundary, not simulated as transient drainage.

Available water is defined relative to the illustrative wilting-point baseline. A deficit above capacity invalidates the planned available-water model; do not silently clamp or continue its unstressed crop-use assumption.

The 0.25-inch crop-use estimate is borrowed from NDSU's North Dakota corn example at 85 degrees F in the ninth week after emergence. Every field, rainfall, irrigation, efficiency and initial-deficit value here is hypothetical.
